newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee not discussing punt-source.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee not discussing punt-source.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee was not discussing the question of the strengthening Irish punt at its meeting on Friday, a committee source said.
Asked whether there had been discussions about the punt, which has risen to close to its 15 percent fluctuation limit within the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism, the source said: "No, No".
The source was speaking as the secretive committee broke up for lunch. The meeting was to continue this afternoon.

The committee of national treasury and central bank officials was meeting amid rife market speculation of a possible revaluation of the punt, but EU officials have said it will focus on a number of issues pertaining to economic and monetary union (EMU).

EU monetary officials on Wednesday said the Irish economy's fundamentals did not justify a revaluation of the punt. "There is no intention whatsoever to talk about the Irish punt," a senior EU official told Reuters.
Instead the meeting was due to discuss various EMU-related issues including relations between EU finance ministers and a future European Central Bank.
It was also slated to discuss the relationship between the euro and currencies such as the dollar and EMU's impact on the International Monetary Fund.
Another point on the agenda was how the monetary committee will eventually evolve into the so-called Economic and Financial Committee after the euro is launched.
